title: Elves Falath Evo Ride Review

takeaways.text: He calls the geometry odd: the raised top tube leaves little seatpost, so at 179 cm he went from size 54 to 52 with a longer stem and was still only just within Elves' seatpost guideline.
Climbing at 350 W he recorded a quicker time than his earlier aero-bike comparison on another day, yet the bike felt cumbersome above about 4–5% and the wide top tube touched his legs when sprinting.

Without pedals but with a computer mount and two bottle cages, his size 52 build weighed about 7.5 kg on 45 mm wheels, 7.7 kg on Elves' 50 mm wheels and just over 8 kg on 69 mm wheels with 30 mm tyres.
On a fast descent he found it among the most stable bikes he has ridden, which he links partly to a longer wheelbase than other aero bikes.
He fitted 30 mm tyres to the 69 mm wheels; they felt slower to him, and he questions the very large tyre gap on an aero frame.
He values Elves' local distributor route for warranty issues and its five-year frame warranty, longer than the three years on the Winspace T1500 he reviewed.
Drawbacks for him: a slammed front end after downsizing, high standover from the raised top tube, and a thick seatpost that made lights and his saddle bag hard to fit.

disclosure: In earlier videos the creator said Elves Australia supplied his pre-production frameset and these wheels and would send a mass-production frame for this review. He says he earns no commission on the wheels; the description links the Australian distributor.
summary: A July 2023 ride review of the custom-painted Falath EVO UCI frameset that replaced the creator's withdrawn pre-production sample, built in size 52 with SRAM Force AXS 1× and Elves' 50 mm wheels. It is not evidence for EVO+ or EXP revisions.
